notes.2: This question was well answered and candidates showed a good understanding of kinematics.
notes.3: While most candidates answered correctly, a few candidates forgot to convert the units of time from minutes to hours. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2019
notes.4: Candidates showed an excellent understanding of the difference between mass and weight.
notes.5: The density problem caused very few problems for the vast majority of candidates.
notes.6: Many candidates answered this question correctly. The most common error was to multiply the 100 N force by 40 cm rather than by (40 + 50) cm.
notes.10: Although the question was answered well by most candidates, a number seemed to take the masses of the two objects to be equal resulting in a final speed of 3.0 m/s.
notes.14: The majority of candidates showed good understanding of pressure and force. However, there were some who thought that the force at the point of the pin was greater than the force on the flat surface.
notes.15: Although the majority of candidates correctly calculated the pressure at the bottom of the mercury column, there were some who forgot to multiply by the g.
notes.16: Almost all candidate correctly answered this question.
notes.18: This question proved challenging with many candidates thinking that the box with the largest temperature rise was the box with the largest thermal capacity.
notes.20: Only stronger candidates answered this correctly. Many candidates did not realise that after a full night in the cold both the steel handlebars and the plastic grips would be at the same temperature.
notes.22: This question caused some minor difficulties, mainly because candidates were under the misconception that shorter wavelength waves diffract more than longer wavelengths.
notes.28: The vast majority of candidates recognised that the positive charge on a rod is due to the loss of electrons.
notes.31: The most common error on this question was to treat the resistors as though they were in series not parallel.
notes.32: Candidates recognised the circuit symbol and knew the role of the diode in a circuit.
